events.text:
⚡️🇺🇸🇮🇱🇵🇸 — President Trump told Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a phone call on Thursday that he wants him to take steps to implement his Gaza peace plan, regardless of whether Netanyahu or his opposition forms the next government, according to two sources cited by Axios.
The roadmap calls for disarming Hamas, demilitarizing Gaza, and transferring responsibility for governing the enclave to a new Palestinian technocratic government. The plan had been on hold for months because of the Israeli elections on October 27, as the administration did not want it to become a politically explosive issue during the campaign.
A year ago, Israel and Hamas agreed to the first phase of Trump's 20-point plan, leading to a ceasefire and the release of the last 20 living hostages. The Board of Peace has been working on an implementation plan, and last July reached a 15-point agreement with Hamas to disarm armed groups and transfer civilian and security control to a new Palestinian government. Since then, Netanyahu's government has largely refused to move forward, mostly for domestic political reasons.
Jared Kushner told Netanyahu during an August visit that Hamas had for the first time agreed to disarm, urging him to test whether the commitment was real. Netanyahu remains extremely skeptical that Hamas will ever demilitarize, saying the group is reconstituting and rearming in Gaza.
Over the past three months, the Board of Peace has worked with the Israeli government and military to refine details and address concerns, with a U.S. official saying the process would be gradual and reconstruction would only begin after progress in disarming Hamas had been verified. The Board unveiled a six-month, $2.45 billion initial recovery plan at the UN General Assembly in September.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Kushner, and envoy Steve Witkoff also participated in the call, which Netanyahu initiated and a source described as constructive. It also addressed the war in Iran. A day later, Tony Blair visited Israel and met with Netanyahu and his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, urging Israeli political leaders to give the plan a chance.
"The implementation will be difficult but we believe it is a good plan for Israel. Nevertheless we can't do it with one hand tied behind our back," a U.S. official said. "We want to move forward collaboratively and we need full cooperation and partnership from the Israeli government."

⚡️🇺🇸🇮🇷 — President Trump stated that new U.S. strikes on Iran are "highly unlikely" provided Tehran makes progress toward a nuclear agreement and reopens the Strait of Hormuz, according to CNN.
Trump told the outlet that any military action depends on whether Iran signs a "very strong agreement," adding, "I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard."
He emphasized American military readiness, noting he has three aircraft carriers in the region that are "fully locked and loaded." He also claimed U.S. forces could destroy 38 Iranian bridges within an hour and that Iran has been reduced to only 10% of its missile capacity and 15% of its drone capabilities.
Despite the warnings, he maintained that renewed strikes are "most likely" not going to be necessary, stating: "They want to make a deal so badly."
